sections.title: Lawsuits Among Believers
observations: Paul addresses the issue of believers taking legal disputes to secular courts rather than resolving them within the church community.
He emphasizes the shame of airing grievances before unbelievers and questions the wisdom of not being able to settle matters among themselves.
The church is called to be a community of reconciliation, reflecting the grace and wisdom of God.

sections.title: The Inheritance of the Kingdom
observations: Paul reminds the Corinthians of their identity in Christ and the transformative power of the Gospel.
He lists various sins that will prevent individuals from inheriting the Kingdom of God, emphasizing the seriousness of sin.
The passage serves as a warning and a call to holiness, reminding believers of their new identity and the need to live accordingly.

sections.title: Sexual Immorality and the Body
observations: Paul discusses the issue of sexual immorality, highlighting its unique nature compared to other sins.
He explains that the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit and should be treated with honor and respect.
This section emphasizes the importance of sexual purity and the believer's responsibility to glorify God with their bodies.

importantVerses.commentary: Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who practice homosexuality will inherit the kingdom of God.

questions: What does it mean for believers to resolve disputes among themselves rather than going to secular courts?
How can the church better reflect the grace and wisdom of God in handling conflicts?
What implications does the idea of the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit have for our daily lives and choices?
